blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 5 sold over 4 months against an average of 27.0 listed, about 21.6 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 3 sold. Condos and townhomes: 20 sold over 4 months against an average of 24.5 listed, about 4.9 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 7 sold.

faq.a: In north-east Burnaby, south of Lougheed Highway between Lougheed Town Centre and Burnaby Lake, named for Government Road and anchored by École Seaforth Elementary at 7881 Government Rd; it is a GVR MLS® sub-area within the City of Burnaby.

faq.q: How did Government Road detached homes do in September 2026?
faq.a: None sold — the SnapStats row shows 24 detached listings and 0 detached solds, so the detached sales ratio is not applicable for the month; the attached side recorded 23 listings and 3 solds, a 13% sales ratio (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which schools serve a Government Road address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. In-area SD41 schools include École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd, and Stoney Creek Community Elementary (K–7), 2740 Beaverbrook Cres, with Cameron Elementary and Burnaby Mountain Secondary on the east side; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

faq.q: How is transit on Government Road?
faq.a: Route 110 runs on Government Road itself, linking Lougheed Station and Production Way–University Station to the east with Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station and Metrotown Station to the west, via Beaverbrook, Eastlake, Brighton, Phillips and Winston.

faq.q: Can a Government Road house lot add units?
faq.a: If the lot is R1, yes — under Burnaby's R1 SSMUH District a house lot may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; corridor parcels in other zones follow their own zone, so confirm the parcel's zone first.
